question: After the stale-policy defect is fixed, should OpenClaw adopt the fail-closed node policy lookup and dual-source denylist contract for permissive full/off execution?
rationale: The correctness repair is mechanical, but permanently making permissive node execution depend on current approval-policy availability and two unioned operator stores is a security-versus-availability product choice.

options.title: Fix then adopt
options.body: Integrate fresh denylist evaluation at every checkpoint, refresh proof, and accept the new authorization contract.

options.title: Consolidate policy ownership
options.body: Keep deny-over-allow but reduce it to one canonical policy store before merge.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Retain the existing allowlist/full/deny model if maintainers do not want the new lookup and policy contract.

recommendation.title: Fix then adopt
recommendation.body: Integrate fresh denylist evaluation at every checkpoint, refresh proof, and accept the new authorization contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership of the overlapping approval revalidation lifecycle makes this the strongest history-backed decision route.
